title: Manage Configuration and IaC
objective: Manage reusable configurations, differences, drift, and multi-account deployments safely.

sections.title: Managing the Desired Configuration State as Code
paragraphs: CloudFormation provisions and configures the AWS resources defined in templates as stacks. Rather than treating manual changes as the authoritative state, operators manage templates, parameters, execution roles, dependencies, and change sets in a reviewable manner.

Before deployment, review the resources that will be created, updated, replaced, or deleted, along with the scope of the impact. Because correct template syntax and safe production changes are separate concerns, combine policy checks with staged deployment.

sources.label: DOP-C02 Exam Guide: Configuration Management and IaC

sections.title: Embedding governance into reusable components
paragraphs: Organization-wide networks, logging, encryption, tags, and backups are provided as reusable modules or templates rather than as copies maintained by each team. Guardrails must detect necessary constraints early while providing an approval path for legitimate exceptions.

When codifying policies, define the target resources, prohibited or required states, evaluation points in time, exceptions, expiration dates, and remediation ownership. A configuration that rejects every change may impede recovery and business continuity instead of improving security.

sources.label: DOP-C02 Exam Guide: Reusable IaC and governance

sections.title: Controlling Multi-Account Deployments Through Permissions and Ordering
paragraphs: In multi-account, multi-Region deployments, use execution roles and trust relationships for each target instead of distributing the management account’s permissions directly to every environment. Separate shared infrastructure, applications, and Region-specific configuration, and clearly define dependency order and the scope of stopping when a failure occurs.

Even for bulk deployments using StackSets and similar tools, verify the target accounts, Regions, concurrency, failure tolerance, and rollback behavior. Before sending a change to all environments at once, validate the expected differences and audit records in a representative environment.

sources.label: DOP-C02 Exam Guide: Multi-Account and Automation

checkpoints.prompt: The person responsible for changing the route configuration of a production VPC with IaC wants to detect unintended resource replacements before applying the changes. Choose the single most appropriate pre-application task.

choices.text: Review the target stack, dependencies, and the differences involving creation, updates, replacements, and deletions before applying the changes.
choices.explanation: This allows impacts that cannot be identified from syntax alone to be checked before application.

choices.text: Make the change in the console first, then update the template.
choices.explanation: The desired state and the actual environment will diverge.

choices.text: Update stacks in all Regions simultaneously without reviewing the differences.
choices.explanation: The scope of impact cannot be controlled.

checkpoints.prompt: The platform team wants to apply encryption and mandatory tags to all applications while handling legally required exceptions. Choose the single most appropriate control design.

choices.text: Define the required state, exception approvals and expiration dates, evaluation points in time, and remediation responsibility in reusable IaC and policies.
choices.explanation: This enables controls and legitimate exceptions to be handled in a traceable manner.

choices.text: Permanently reject all changes without considering exceptions.
choices.explanation: This could hinder recovery and business requirements.

choices.text: Manually duplicate custom templates for each team.
choices.explanation: This can lead to inconsistent controls and missed updates.

checkpoints.prompt: The person responsible for distributing a common audit log configuration to multiple accounts wants to limit the impact of failures. Select the one most appropriate deployment approach.

choices.text: Share administrator permissions across all accounts and deploy to all environments simultaneously.
choices.explanation: This eliminates permission boundaries and expands the impact.

choices.text: Define the target accounts, execution role, dependency order, concurrency, and failure tolerance, then validate the configuration in a representative environment before deploying it.
choices.explanation: This lets you control the permissions and failure scope of the bulk deployment.

choices.text: Do not record the deployment results.
choices.explanation: This makes it impossible to identify failures or decide whether to rerun the deployment.
